chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Hilal, from Uqba ibn Khalid, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) ruled regarding pre-emption (shuf'ah) between partners in lands and dwellings, and said: 'No harm and no causing harm.' And he said: 'When the markings are marked and the boundaries are defined, then there is no pre-emption.'

key_terms.الشُّفْعَةِ: Pre-emption; the right of a partner or co-owner to purchase another's share before it is sold to an outsider.
key_terms.الْأُرُفُ: Markings; physical signs or boundaries set on the land.
key_terms.الْحُدُودُ: Boundaries; the defined limits of the property.
key_terms.لَا ضَرَرَ: No harm; a fundamental legal maxim meaning one should not cause harm to others.
key_terms.لَا ضِرَارَ: No suffering harm; the reciprocal right to not be harmed by others.

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on pre-emption (shuf'ah) in shared property and when does it end?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi grounds the right of pre-emption (shuf'ah) in the Prophet’s judicial practice, linking it to the broader principle of 'la darar wa la dirar' (no harm) to prevent injustice among co-owners. Shia jurists emphasize that this right is contingent upon the property remaining undivided; once boundaries (hudud) are clearly marked and established, the right of pre-emption ceases, ensuring legal certainty and preventing perpetual disputes.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Al Husayn, from Muhamma Bin Abdullah Bin Hilal, from Uqba Bin Khalid, 
from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> judged with the pre-emption between the partners regarding the lands and the dwellings, and said: ‘Neither harm nor suffer harm’. And he<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘When the markings are marked and the boundaries are defined, so there is no pre-emption’.
en.sarwar: 4. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Muhammad ibn ‘Abd Allah ibn Hilal from ‘Uqbah ibn Khalid who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘

The Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, issued a judgment in favor of al- Shuf’ (one’s rights of pre-emption) in the case of partners in the ownership of land and houses, saying, “Harming and causing harm because of suffering harm is not lawful.” He (the Messenger of Allah) also said, “Once division takes place and boundaries are set al-Shuf’ (one’s rights of pre-emption) ceases to exist.’””
